newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybeans end mixed in slow trading.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybeans end mixed in slow trading.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mixed in slow trading on Monday with later-maturing contracts up while early-maturing contracts ended down, traders said.
The most active September 1997 contract ended at an intraday high of 3,427 yuan ($413) per tonne, rising 97 yuan. It opened at 3,400 and hit a low of 3,390.
March was unchanged at 3,130, May fell 102 to 3,300, July was down 20 to 3,395, November rose 61 to 3,401 and January 1998 contract was up 90 to 3,440.
Combined volume fell to 12,500 tonnes from 36,600.
Soybeans opened higher and later-maturing contracts rose further to end at their intra-day highs while early-maturing contracts ended down on profit-taking following heavy gains in the past week.
"Improved fundamentals encouraged investors to build long positions in the later-maturing contracts, which are likely to rise further in the next few days," one trader said.

But traders said sharp rises were unlikely in the short term given a lack of market-moving news. "Thin volume indicated institutions stayed on the sidelines and soybeans will not rise sharply in the next few days," a second trader said.
